def_en: to make a device start working
note_ru: Turn on the light, но с местоимением — turn it on, не «turn on it».
example: Can you turn on the heating?

examples_extra.en: I turned the TV on and fell asleep.
Turn it on and wait a minute.

def_en: to make a device stop working
note_ru: Свет, воду, телефон — всё turn off. Switch off — то же самое.
example: Please turn off your phones.

examples_extra.en: Did you turn off the oven?
Turn the music off, it's late.

def_en: to place clothes on your body
note_ru: Put on — действие, wear — состояние: put on a coat, потом wear a coat.
example: Put on a warm jacket, it's cold.

examples_extra.en: She put on her glasses and read the note.
examples_extra.ru: Она надела очки и прочитала записку.

examples_extra.en: Put your shoes on, we're leaving.

def_en: to remove clothes; to leave the ground
note_ru: Два главных смысла: take off your shoes и the plane takes off.
example: Take off your coat, it's warm inside.

examples_extra.en: The plane took off on time.
He took off his hat and smiled.

def_en: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
note_ru: Wake up — проснуться, get up — встать с кровати. Это разные моменты утра.
example: I woke up before the alarm.

examples_extra.en: Don't wake up the baby.
She wakes up at six every day.
examples_extra.ru: Она просыпается в шесть каждый день.

note_ru: Проснулся в семь, встал в восемь: woke up at seven, got up at eight.
example: I get up at seven on weekdays.
example_ru: По будням я встаю в семь.

examples_extra.en: He got up late and missed the bus.
examples_extra.ru: Он поздно встал и опоздал на автобус.

examples_extra.en: Time to get up, breakfast is ready.

note_ru: Go out — не просто «выйти», а «пойти развеяться»: в кафе, в кино, к друзьям.
example: Let's go out for dinner tonight.

examples_extra.en: They go out every Friday.
I'm too tired to go out.
examples_extra.ru: Я слишком устал, чтобы куда-то идти.

note_ru: Come back — сюда, go back — туда: come back home, go back to the office.
example: What time will you come back?

examples_extra.en: She came back with two coffees.
Come back soon, we miss you.

note_ru: Look for — процесс поиска, find — результат: I looked for the keys and found them.
example: I'm looking for my glasses.

examples_extra.en: She's looking for a new flat.
What are you looking for?

def_en: to put on clothes to see if they fit
note_ru: Try on — про одежду и обувь. Просто «попробовать» еду — try без on.
example: Can I try on these jeans?

examples_extra.en: Try it on before you buy it.
She tried on five dresses.

def_en: to clean the dishes after a meal
note_ru: Британцы говорят wash up или do the dishes. «Мыть руки» — просто wash your hands.
example: I'll cook if you wash up.
example_ru: Я готовлю, если ты моешь посуду.

examples_extra.en: Whose turn is it to wash up?
He washed up and went to bed.
examples_extra.ru: Он помыл посуду и пошёл спать.

note_ru: «Я хочу есть» — I'm hungry, а не «I want to eat» в каждой фразе.
example: I'm really hungry, let's eat.

examples_extra.en: The kids get hungry after school.

note_ru: «Хочу пить» — I'm thirsty. Дословного «я жаждущий» по-русски нет, поэтому слово часто забывают.
example: I'm so thirsty after the run.
example_ru: Я так хочу пить после пробежки.

examples_extra.en: Salty food makes you thirsty.

note_ru: Tired of — «надоело»: I'm tired of waiting. Это не про усталость тела.
example: You look tired. Go to bed.

examples_extra.en: I'm tired of this rain.

note_ru: Angry with a person, angry about a thing: злюсь на него — angry with him.
example: She was angry with me for being late.
example_ru: Она злилась на меня за опоздание.

examples_extra.en: Don't be angry about the mess.

note_ru: Scared of: боюсь собак — I'm scared of dogs. Afraid of — то же, чуть формальнее.
example: I'm scared of spiders.

examples_extra.en: Don't be scared, the dog is friendly.

def_en: feeling that something is not interesting
note_ru: Bored — мне скучно, boring — сам предмет скучный. «I'm boring» значит «я зануда»!
example: I'm bored. Let's do something.

examples_extra.en: The kids got bored after an hour.

note_ru: Пара к bored: фильм boring, поэтому я bored. Перепутать — классика.
example: The lecture was so boring.

examples_extra.en: It's a boring little town.

note_ru: Surprised at или by: удивлён результату — surprised at the result.
example: I was surprised at the price.

examples_extra.en: She wasn't surprised by the news.

def_en: feeling pleased about something done well
note_ru: Proud of: горжусь тобой — I'm proud of you. Предлог только of.
example: We're proud of our team.

examples_extra.en: She's proud of her garden.

note_ru: Только после глагола: I'm glad. «A glad person» не говорят — тогда happy.
example: I'm glad you came.

examples_extra.en: Glad to hear the good news!

note_ru: Ставится в конец: Say it again. «Again say» — типичная русская калька.
example: Could you say that again, please?
example_ru: Не могли бы вы повторить ещё раз?

examples_extra.en: It's raining again.

note_ru: Already — в утверждениях, yet — в вопросах и отрицаниях: I've already eaten.
example: I've already seen this film.

examples_extra.en: It's already dark outside.

def_en: until now — in questions and negatives
note_ru: Have you eaten yet? — «уже». I haven't eaten yet — «ещё не». Всегда в конце.
example: Have you finished yet?

examples_extra.en: The parcel hasn't arrived yet.

note_ru: Still — до глагола: He still works there. Не путать с yet: still — продолжается, yet — ещё не случилось.
example: Are you still at work?

examples_extra.en: I still remember my first lesson.
examples_extra.ru: Я до сих пор помню свой первый урок.
